findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving the service account near-administrative control over compute, storage, and serverless resources. Compromise of this user's credentials would allow data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and arbitrary EC2/Lambda execution.

A permanent IAM access key is created in Terraform for a highly privileged user; the secret is stored in Terraform state in plaintext (no pgp_key is set), so anyone with state access obtains long-lived admin-ish AWS credentials. Prefer IAM roles / temporary credentials.
Because no pgp_key is supplied, the access key's secret (and ses_smtp_password) are written unencrypted to the Terraform state file, leaking credentials to anyone who can read state.
A long-lived IAM user with broad permissions is created with no MFA requirement or permissions boundary, relying solely on static keys for access to wildcard privileges.
The output svc_deploy_key_material exposes the access key secret material and is not marked sensitive, so it is printed in CLI output and CI logs where it can be harvested.
